questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A student was asked to draw a plan diagram of the plant tissue shown in the photomicrograph and to annotate two observable features. What are the correct annotations?

options.A: epidermis darkly stained layer of cells, xylem hollow vessels
options.B: epidermis formed of single layer of cells, xylem strengthened by lignin
options.C: phloem small cells, xylem empty cells to transport water
options.D: vascular bundles arranged in a regular pattern, xylem large dead cells

options.A: the inability to cut very thin sections

The table shows the results of the tests. reagent observation ethanol and water white emulsion Benedict’s solution brick red precipitate Biuret blue colour Which row shows the molecules found in the plant extract? protein fatty acids reducing sugar
Glycogen is a polymer of glucose. Which description summarises its structure?

options.A: α-glucose joined by glycosidic bonds involving carbons 1 and 4
options.B: α-alpha glucose joined by glycosidic bonds involving carbons 1, 4 and 6
options.C: β-beta glucose joined by glycosidic bonds involving carbons 1 and 4
options.D: β-beta glucose joined by glycosidic bonds involving carbons 1, 4 and 6

questions.questionText: Glucose in urine can be detected using a biochemical test. When the end of a test strip, which is impregnated with the enzyme glucose oxidase, is dipped into urine, the development of a blue colour indicates that glucose is present. This is a reliable test that people with diabetes can carry out at home. Which feature of the enzyme makes this test so reliable?

options.C: It lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
options.D: It only works at low pH range.

questions.questionText: What is the role of cholesterol in the cell surface membrane?

options.D: to regulate fluidity of the membrane

questions.questionText: A peptide consists of ten amino acids of four different kinds. What is the theoretical minimum number of different tRNA molecules required to translate the mRNA for this peptide?
Which statements about tRNA structure are correct?
Which statements describe why a large animal has had to evolve a transport system?
Which row identifies the tissue that contains the Casparian strip and the molecule forming this strip? tissue molecule
Which of the following are included in the apoplast pathway?
Which statement explains why the circumference (girth) of a tree is less in the middle of the day than at night?

options.A: Mineral uptake by the root hair cells decreases during the night because root pressure has decreased.
options.B: Stomata close during the night and there is a build-up of water in the vascular tissue within the stem.
options.C: The phloem sieve tubes fill with dissolved solutes because the translocation rate is reduced at night.
options.D: There is less tension in the xylem vessels at night because the rate of transpiration is at a minimum.

The graph shows the amount of antibody produced in response to an antigen. concentration of antibody in the blood 0 10 20 30 40 time in days first exposure to an antigen From the graph, which statement is correct?

options.A: It takes 25 days to achieve active immunity.

questions.questionText: Which of the following two diseases are caused by viruses?
Cholera is no longer common in many countries. What is the reason for this?

options.A: education of the citizens about the spread of the disease
options.B: routine vaccination by local health authorities
options.C: treatment of water supplies and separate sewage treatment
options.D: treatment of water to control mosquitoes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a food web. seagull starfish herbivorous molluscs sea urchin barnacles crustaceans zooplankton algae detritus How many trophic levels are represented in the food web?
What is the role of decomposers in the nitrogen cycle?

options.A: They convert proteins to ammonium compounds.
options.C: They oxidise ammonium compounds to nitrites.

questions.questionText: Why could only 4% of the energy from sunlight be fixed by producers during photosynthesis?

options.A: A lot of energy is lost as energy passes from one trophic level to the next in food chains.
options.B: A lot of sunlight reflects off clouds, is absorbed by pond water or does not strike chloroplasts.
options.C: Some energy passes from dead plants to decomposers such as bacteria and fungi.
options.D: Some parts of plants are not eaten or cannot be digested by herbivores.
